research_concepts: offensive five (lineup) change from substitution rotation intervals
shot mix: rim share, three-point attempt share, mid-range share, from play-by-play shot distance
positive control / design sensitivity for personnel effects
confounding by game state, opponent, fatigue and player talent
methodological_questions: Does a within-team, within-game before/after comparison of adjacent stints detect a shift in shot mix when the five changes?
How should a meaningful lineup change be defined, given that every substitution changes the five?
Does the shift scale with how different the incoming and outgoing players' shot profiles are (dose-response)?
How can personnel effects be separated from score, clock, period, opponent lineup and fatigue?
Which placebo (no-personnel-change) events show the design does not manufacture shifts?
What minimum detectable effect is available, and does it cover the sub-1pp shifts seen in earlier work?

historical_evidence.finding: Shot mix when the opposing rim big is off the floor: DRIVE +0.82pp (SE 0.25), POST_UP +0.43pp, 3PA -1.79pp (SE 0.31), rim <=4ft +0.12pp (t=+0.4), PPP +0.008 (t=+1.1), N=1.07M possessions. The record notes that sub-1pp mix shifts will not carry a paper. Its limitations are small sample and SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER.

The connector lineup-lift claim was a null (BOTH_NULL on-off PPP, n=73). The apparent lineup ORtg lift disappeared after a TALENT control (p=0.51), which is a talent confound. Limited by confounding and small sample.

The PULL_UP exposure effect changed from -0.0255 with lineup fixed effects to -0.0063 without them. A same-shooter placebo on other play types gave about -0.0075, consistent with a shooter-level confound. Lineup and shooter composition materially change estimates.
Lineup-specific suppression cells (n>=30) were reported with no placebo or matching. Later sequence work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts. Flagged PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE.

Descriptive after-timeout play-type shifts (POST_UP +2.406, SPOT_UP +2.333) were measured against same game-offense-period-minute comparisons. It uses the reconstructed-lineup possession dataset, and the matching-on-game-period-minute design is a possible template.
Descriptive play-type mix shifts by halftime margin, crunch time and after runs. There were no inferential tests, and the OTHER label is noisy. Shot mix moves with game state.
The within-game exposure slope was near zero (-0.0019, SE 0.0019). Only PULL_UP survived Holm. Limited by insufficient exposure, label error and low measurement reliability.
Team-season heterogeneity in halftime adaptation was not distinguishable from sampling noise (split-half r=-0.026, 120 team-seasons). Team-level trait estimates can be unreliable.
The adapter PPP lift failed falsification tests. The record lists label error and selection or regression to the mean (and MECHANICAL_FLOOR) as limitations.
On-ball scheme labels could not be built at usable rates (14.9% and 3.3% labelled; switches_on unpopulated). Derived tactical labels from the matchup feed are unreliable.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Reading a lineup-level effect without lineup fixed effects or a same-shooter placebo
failed_approaches.why: C_artifact: the effect shrank from -0.0255 to -0.0063 and the placebo play types showed a similar slope (shooter-level confound).

failed_approaches.what_what_failed: Attributing lineup lift to one player type without controlling for talent
failed_approaches.why: The lift was a talent confound (p=0.51 after TALENT; B_powered_null).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Lineup-specific cells reported with no placebo or matching
failed_approaches.why: PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE; similar gaps were later treated as artifacts.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Detecting sub-1pp shot-mix shifts, even at N=1.07M possessions
failed_approaches.why: Rim share +0.12pp with t=+0.4; the record calls the result weak and small, with SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER as the risk.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Labelling on-ball scheme from the NBA matchup feed
failed_approaches.why: A_unanswerable: confident label rates were 14.9% and 3.3%, and switches_on was unpopulated.

evidence_establishes: No retrieved record tests whether a change of the offensive five moves shot mix, so no earlier result is directly on point.
Earlier work found shot-mix shifts that follow lineup-related changes (for example 3PA -1.79pp when the opposing big is off the floor), but these are opponent-side lineup effects.
Lineup composition, player talent and game state have produced confounded or artifactual estimates in earlier work (FAM:SF-TMP-009, FAM:SF-APPS-087).
A lineup-composition dataset built from play-by-play already exists in the project (the reconstructed-lineup possession dataset cited by FAM:SF-TMP-023).
Labelled or derived tactical classes (OTHER, scheme labels) have been unreliable, whereas the shot-distance fields were not flagged as a problem in these records.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether swapping offensive personnel produces a shot-mix shift of any given size.
The magnitude and variance of shot-mix shifts after substitutions, or the exposure needed for power.
Whether a lineup-change design can reject a placebo (non-personnel) change.
Whether the design is sensitive to sub-1pp shifts. FAM:SF34 suggests such shifts are hard to resolve.
own_inferences: A substitution that swaps a rim-running big for a wing is almost mechanically expected to move rim and three-point shares, so a well-defined personnel contrast is very likely to yield a detectable shift. This is an expectation, not a recorded result.

As worded, the claim is partly circular. If 'changing the five' includes any substitution, the shift will be heterogeneous and averages may be small. The positive control is meaningful only with a pre-specified, role-based contrast and a dose-response check.

A positive control on large personnel contrasts shows sensitivity only to large effects. It does not show the design can detect the sub-1pp effects in FAM:SF34, so the claim 'the design can detect personnel effects' must be scoped to the minimum detectable effect.

Substitution timing is endogenous (fouls, fatigue, score, timeouts, matchups), so naive before/after differences confound personnel with state. Within-game adjacent-stint matching, game-state covariates and a dose-response on held-out player profiles mitigate this.
Player profiles used for the dose-response must come from data not used in the outcome (for example prior-season or other-game data) to avoid circularity.
uncertainties: The exact format of the shot-distance fields and the lineup reconstruction accuracy are not verified here (substitution intervals and starters exist, but reconstruction error rates are not recorded in retrieval).
Possession counts per stint, and hence power per lineup change, are unknown until the data are inspected.
No retrieved record gives a variance estimate for stint-level shot-mix shifts.
Whether free-throw and garbage-time possessions are handled consistently is unknown.
Retrieval returned no directly relevant prior study, so prior-work coverage is incomplete in this setting.

historical_effect.explanation: No retrieved work answers the question directly, so the decision is not driven by a prior answer. The history did change the design. FAM:SF-TMP-009 and FAM:SF-APPS-087 show that lineup and talent confounds create artifacts and that placebos are required. FAM:SF34 shows sub-1pp shifts are hard to detect, so the claim is scoped to a minimum detectable effect and to large role-based contrasts. FAM:SF-APPS-058 and FAM:SF-APPM-021 support using raw shot-distance zones rather than derived play-type labels. This moves the decision from a plain 'proceed' to 'proceed_with_changes'.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved family tested whether changing the offensive five moves shot mix. Related work concerns opponent lineup effects (FAM:SF34, inconclusive) and lineup or talent confounds (FAM:SF-TMP-009 artifact, FAM:SF-APPS-087 rejected). That work informs design choices only and does not answer the question.

risks.text: Substitutions are endogenous to score, foul trouble, fatigue, opponent lineup, clock and period. Player talent and shooter selection drive lineup effects (FAM:SF-TMP-009, FAM:SF-APPS-087).
Without a no-change placebo, any before/after shift could come from the stint boundary itself (fatigue, timeouts, clock). A placebo must be run on same-five boundaries.
Many specific five-man contrasts will have few possessions per stint. FAM:SF34 shows sub-1pp shifts are not resolved even at N=1.07M. Power must be stated as a minimum detectable effect.
Several shot-mix measures and role-contrast definitions could produce spurious significance if not pre-specified.
If the dose-response profiles use the same games as the outcome, the predicted shift is circular. Profiles must come from held-out data.
Lineup reconstruction from substitution intervals can misassign players around timeouts and quarter breaks, which attenuates estimates.
Swapping the only big for a wing mechanically moves rim share. The test then confirms the obvious and cannot show sensitivity to subtle effects.
Shot mix trends across the three seasons and between regular season and playoffs, and playoff rotations differ.

design.estimand: Positive-control estimand: the mean within-game change in shot-mix shares (primary: share of FGA at <=4 ft; secondary: three-point attempt share; mid-range share) between the possessions of consecutive stints, comparing (a) substitutions with a pre-defined large role contrast (a rim-big replaced by a non-big or vice versa, top tercile of predicted profile change) against (b) placebo boundaries with the same five. The dose-response estimand is the slope of observed shift on predicted shift from out-of-sample player profiles.
design.unit: Team-stint pairs (adjacent offensive stints within a game), with possessions as the observation level and clustering by team-game.
design.sample: NBA 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular seasons (primary); playoffs reported separately and excluded from the primary. Exclude garbage time, end-of-period heaves, and stints under a pre-set minimum of possessions (for example 6 per side). Lineups from rotation intervals, checked against play-by-play substitution events.
design.power: Before analysis, count eligible stint pairs and possessions per role-contrast class. Report the minimum detectable effect at 80% power from the empirical variance, using the split-half or season-to-season stability of the shift. Claim detection only for effects above that threshold. State explicitly that sensitivity to sub-1pp effects (cf. FAM:SF34) is not claimed unless the MDE is below 1pp.
design.controls: Adjacent-stint matching within the same game, period and opponent. Covariates: score margin, clock bucket, period, opponent lineup (rim-big present or absent), home/away, days of rest. Player-profile model from prior-season or held-out games only (no overlap with outcome games). Lineup or team-season fixed effects, and a talent control (cf. FAM:SF-TMP-009, FAM:SF-APPS-087).
design.falsification: Placebo A: pseudo-substitution boundaries (same timestamps, same five). Placebo B: stoppage and quarter boundaries with no change of the five. Placebo C: permuting the role contrast labels across substitutions within game-period. Negative control: contrasts that swap players with near-identical predicted profiles should show about zero shift. The positive control counts as passed only if the primary contrast beats all placebos and the dose-response slope is positive.
design.multiplicity: One primary outcome (rim share) and one primary contrast. Secondary outcomes (three-point share, mid-range share) are tested with Holm correction at family-wise alpha=0.05. Role-contrast definitions are fixed in advance and not tuned.
design.decision_rule: Supported if (1) the primary contrast shift in rim share has a CI excluding 0 in the predicted direction, (2) the dose-response slope is positive with CI excluding 0, (3) the placebo shifts are indistinguishable from 0 and smaller in magnitude than the primary shift. Rejected only if the MDE is small relative to the expected shift and the CI is tightly around 0. Artifact if placebos show shifts comparable to the primary effect or the effect vanishes after fixed effects. Otherwise inconclusive. Replicate the direction in each of the three seasons.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game play-by-play, rotation intervals, starters and box-score summary for 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25 regular season and playoffs, as available on 2026-11-02. Freeze the extract and record file hashes and the lineup-reconstruction version before analysis.

methodological_questions: Can a within-team design detect that changing the offensive five shifts shot mix?
How should lineup change be defined from substitution rotation intervals and what is the exposure per lineup?
How to separate personnel effects from confounding by opponent, game state, score, clock and period?
What sample size and power are available for five-man lineup comparisons?

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Changing the offensive five itself moves shot mix, showing the design can detect personnel effects.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
